selected_script.angle: Stop attacking dried bug splatter on the windshield with plain water and a gas-station paper towel that just drags sticky residue across the glass; use the Chemical Guys kit’s Streak-Free Glass Cleaner and blue microfiber towel for a clearer same-spot clean.
selected_script.hook: I tried wiping this bug splatter with a wet paper towel, and it just smeared across the windshield.

timeline.0-3s: Extreme close-up on dried bug splatter and dusty film stuck to a car windshield; a hand uses a wet paper towel, but the mark barely lifts and starts spreading.
timeline.3-6s: The same paper towel keeps rubbing harder in small circles, leaving cloudy streaks, torn paper lint, and a wider smeared patch on the same glass area.
timeline.6-10s: The Chemical Guys kit enters naturally beside the windshield, showing the camo bucket and recognizable bottles; the hand uses the Streak-Free Glass Cleaner and blue microfiber towel on the same smear, then tilts the phone to show a clean cleared section next to the still-dirty edge for proof, with a casual spoken CTA.

scenes.promptText: Create one complete approximately 10-second vertical TikTok-style UGC cleaning ad in 9:16, realistic handheld phone-shot style, natural driveway daylight, no polished studio look. Timeline: 0-3s: start with an extreme close-up of a credible cleaning pain on a car windshield: dried bug splatter, dusty road film, and a small sticky mark on the glass. A regular hand tries the familiar ordinary method, a damp paper towel with plain water, rubbing the spot. The paper towel visibly fails: the bug mark does not come off cleanly and begins to drag into a cloudy smear. Do not show the product yet. 3-6s: stay on the same windshield spot and continue the failed method. The hand rubs harder in short frustrated circles, the wet paper towel wrinkles and leaves tiny lint bits, the smear gets wider and hazier, and the effort looks annoying but realistic. Keep the camera very close so the viewer sees streaks, residue, and failed wiping clearly. 6-10s: the Chemical Guys 16-Piece Car Washing and Interior Detailing Kit enters naturally at the lower edge of the same driveway scene, not as a perfect product hero shot. Preserve exact product identity from the reference images: the blue, white, black, and gray camo 4.5 gallon bucket with the large circular Chemical Guys logo, multicolor Chemical Guys bottles, blue microfiber towels, green chenille mitt, green and black TORQ Foam Blaster with clear reservoir, brush, applicators, and correct proportions, colors, materials, label placement, shapes, textures, and visible structure. A hand picks up the real Streak-Free Glass Cleaner spray bottle and a blue microfiber towel from the kit, sprays the same smeared windshield area lightly, then wipes with the microfiber in a normal human motion. Show real cleaning action only: the residue gradually lifts through wiping, no magical instant disappearance, no exaggerated chemical effects, no glowing foam, no fake steam. Finish by tilting the phone to show credible proof on the same glass: a clear wiped section beside a still-dirty edge or faint before/after boundary, with natural reflections sharper on the cleaned area. End with a casual spoken line only: “Way better — check out the kit.” No subtitles, no stickers, no text overlays, no UI, no watermark, no invented accessories, no extra buttons, no extra lights, no altered packaging, no product drift, no changing the product category, no exaggerated results.
